chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The countrymen of al-Anbār met him as he was proceeding towards Syria, so they walked on foot before him and ran in front of him. He asked: What is this that you have done?
They replied: It is a custom of ours by which we show respect to our chiefs.

He said (peace be upon him): By Allah, your chiefs do not benefit from this! Indeed, you burden yourselves in your worldly life, and by it you suffer in your hereafter. How loss-making is the hardship whose consequence is punishment, and how profitable is ease with which there is safety from the Fire.

key_terms.دَهَاقِينُ: countrymen or inhabitants of a specific place

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on excessive displays of respect to leaders?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiqued the people of al-Anbār for their excessive, self-imposed physical exertion—walking barefoot and rushing ahead—to honor their leaders, viewing it as a futile display of 'custom' rather than genuine reverence. He highlighted the spiritual cost of this practice, arguing that the worldly burden of such ostentatious respect leads to eternal suffering, whereas simplicity and ease secure safety from the Hellfire.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 37. Once Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, was proceeding towards Syria when the countrymen of al-Anbār met him.
Seeing him they began to walk on foot and then ran in front of him. He enquired why they were doing so
and they replied that this was the way they respected their chiefs.

Then he said: By Allāh, this does not benefit your chiefs. You are belabouring yourself in this world and earning misery for the next world by it. How harmful is the labour in whose wake there is punishment and how profitable is the case with which there is deliverance from the Fire (of Hell).
